The '''[[2013–14 AHL season|2013–14]] [[Grand Rapids Griffins]] [[season (sports)|season]]''' was the franchise's [[List of Grand Rapids Griffins seasons|13th season]] in the [[American Hockey League]].

==Off-season==
Following the Grand Rapids Griffins' [[Calder Cup]]-winning season last year, several of the players were called up to the [[Detroit Red Wings]], including forwards [[Joakim Andersson]] and [[Tomáš Tatar]]; and defensemen [[Danny DeKeyser]], [[Brian Lashoff]] and [[Brendan Smith (ice hockey)|Brendan Smith]].<ref name="WS0930">{{cite news |last=Duff |first=Bob |title=AHL stars shine in Windsor |work=[[Windsor Star]] |date=September 30, 2013 |url=https://windsorstar.com/sports/stars+shine+Windsor/8976180/story.html |accessdate=October 16, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017041710/http://www.windsorstar.com/sports/stars+shine+Windsor/8976180/story.html |archivedate=2013-10-17 |url-status=live }}</ref> There was a great deal of roster movements between the two teams throughout the off-season, with some players getting repeatedly called back and forth, which meant Griffins coach [[Jeff Blashill]] could not finalize the roster or [[Power play (sporting term)|power play]] and [[Short-handed|penalty kill]] teams until just before the regular season began.<ref name="Wallner1004">{{cite news|last=Wallner |first=Peter J. |title=Ready or not, Grand Rapids Griffins open season tonight and coach Jeff Blashill offers no excuses |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=October 4, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/10/ready_or_not_grand_rapids_grif.html |accessdate=October 16, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052842/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/10/ready_or_not_grand_rapids_grif.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Ten of the 20 players on Detroit's starting roster had played with Grand Rapids the previous year.<ref>{{cite web|last=Katje |first=Jonathan |title=Detroit Red Wings: 8 Prospects To Watch During 2013-14 Season |publisher=Rant Sports |date=October 4, 2013 |url=http://www.rantsports.com/nhl/2013/10/04/detroit-red-wings-8-prospects-to-watch-during-2013-14-season/ |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924090242/http://www.rantsports.com/nhl/2013/10/04/detroit-red-wings-8-prospects-to-watch-during-2013-14-season/ |archivedate=September 24, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> Other Griffins departures included defenseman [[Chad Billins]],<ref name="Wallner0922" /> goaltender [[Jordan Pearce]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Katje |first=Jonathan |title=Detroit Red Wings: Goaltender Tom McCollum Sticking Around After All |publisher=Rant Sports |date=July 4, 2013 |url=http://www.rantsports.com/nhl/2013/07/04/detroit-red-wings-goaltender-tom-mccollum-sticking-around-after-all/ |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130706205507/http://www.rantsports.com/nhl/2013/07/04/detroit-red-wings-goaltender-tom-mccollum-sticking-around-after-all/ |archivedate=July 6, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> and forwards [[Jan Muršak]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Wallner |first=Peter J. |title=Jan Mursak ends stay with Detroit organization, signs deal with Russian team Amur |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=May 7, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/05/jan_mursak_to_end_stay_with_de.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052837/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/05/jan_mursak_to_end_stay_with_de.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Francis Paré]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Paré, Sexton and Seiga sign contracts |date=July 8, 2013 |language=Finnish |publisher=[[HC TPS]] |url=http://hc.tps.fi/uutiset-ajankohtaista-pare_sexton_ja_seigo_tpsaan |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017055209/http://hc.tps.fi/uutiset-ajankohtaista-pare_sexton_ja_seigo_tpsaan |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Winger [[Cory Emmerton]] began the regular season with Detroit after [[Patrick Eaves]] was placed on long-term [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Khan |first=Ansar |title=Cory Emmerton to start season with Red Wings after Patrick Eaves placed on long-term injured reserve |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=September 30, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/cory_emmerton_to_start_season.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017054352/http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/cory_emmerton_to_start_season.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Gustav Nyquist]] was sent down to Grand Rapids from Detroit, but was not expected to remain there long. The move was primarily intended to keep the team under its [[salary cap]], since Nyquist could be transferred without having to clear [[Waivers (NHL)|waivers]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Khan |first=Ansar |title=Red Wings assign forward Gustav Nyquist, goaltender Petr Mrazek to Grand Rapids Griffins |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=September 30, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/red_wings_assign_forward_gusta.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052830/http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/red_wings_assign_forward_gusta.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Griffins signed several new skaters during the off-season, giving the roster a mix of veterans and young prospects. New additions included goaltender Jared Coreau; defensemen [[Alexey Marchenko]], [[Richard Nedomlel]] and [[Xavier Ouellet]]; forwards [[Martin Frk]], [[David McIntyre]] and [[Marek Tvrdoň|Marek Tvrdon]]. McIntyre was the only one of the seven with previous [[American Hockey League]] experience.<ref name="Wallner0927">{{cite news|last=Wallner |first=Peter J. |title=Prized first-year forwards look for opportunities with Grand Rapids Griffins |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=September 27, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/prized_frontliners_look_for_op.html |accessdate=October 16, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052834/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/prized_frontliners_look_for_op.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> The team re-signed defensemen [[Nathan Paetsch]] and [[Brennan Evans]], and forwards [[Triston Grant]] and team captain [[Jeff Hoggan]],<ref name="Wallner0922">{{cite news|last=Wallner |first=Peter J. |title=Grand Rapids Griffins to open camp, here are main storylines to follow |date=September 22, 2013 |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_set_to_o.html |accessdate=October 16, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052823/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_set_to_o.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as several skaters who had played only a handful of games the previous year, including center [[Calle Järnkrok]], winger [[Teemu Pulkkinen]],<ref name="Wallner0927" /> and defenseman [[Ryan Sproul]].<ref name="Wallner1004" />

After a training camp that began September 23 at [[Van Andel Arena]],<ref name="Wallner0922" /> the Griffins played a pair of off-season games against the [[Lake Erie Monsters]], although eight of their players were absent due to a call-up to Detroit.<ref>{{cite news|last=Khan |first=Ansar |title=Red Wings recall eight players from Grand Rapids for Saturday's preseason finale in Toronto |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |date=September 27, 2013 |url=http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/red_wings_recall_eight_players.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017054354/http://www.mlive.com/redwings/index.ssf/2013/09/red_wings_recall_eight_players.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Grand Rapids won the first game 3–2 in a shootout, with Frk scoring the sole shootout goal and McCollum making 36 saves and stopped five shootout shots.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rapids Griffins win shootout in exhibition against Lake Erie |date=September 18, 2013 |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_win_shoo.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017052827/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_win_shoo.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Lake Erie won the second game in a 2–0 shutout.<ref>{{cite news|title=Grand Rapids Griffins blanked in second exhibition game |date=September 30, 2013 |publisher=[[Booth Newspapers]] |url=http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_blanked_1.html |accessdate=October 15, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017054348/http://www.mlive.com/griffins/index.ssf/2013/09/grand_rapids_griffins_blanked_1.html |archivedate=October 17, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Center [[Landon Ferraro]], the team's third-highest score the previous year, suffered a foot injury during the off-season that kept him out of the first two weeks of the regular season.<ref name="Wallner1004" />

==Regular season==
On October 4, the Grand Rapids Griffins won their season opener against the [[Rochester Americans]] by a score of 8–1, setting a franchise record for largest margin of victory in a season debut, breaking the previous record of four goals in 2004. [[Gustav Nyquist]] and [[Adam Almquist]] led the scoring with three points apiece.
